title: A saga that fails at the third of five steps
request:
a five-step saga driven in one command, failing at step three

./your_program.sh saga
init ["reserve","charge","pack","ship","notify"]
run 3
ledger
note: The ledger is the whole specification of this stage: `do:reserve`, `do:charge`, `undo:charge`, `undo:reserve`. Note that `pack` appears nowhere. It failed, so it never completed, and compensating a step that did not happen is how a saga refunds money it never took.

title: A compensation retried after it failed
request:
one compensation that fails, then succeeds, then is retried once more

./your_program.sh saga
init ["reserve","charge","ship"]
step reserve ok
step charge fail
compensate reserve fail
compensate reserve ok
compensate reserve ok
ledger
note: Both halves matter. A compensation that fails must stay at the head of the queue, because skipping it leaves the reservation held for ever; and the retry that eventually lands must be idempotent, because the orchestrator cannot tell a lost answer from a step that never ran.
